Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one fixed full-body combat sprite for an existing 2D fighting-game character.
Input image 1 is the original Silent Hill 4 male Sniffer Dog model and controls identity and anatomy. Input image 2 is the project's existing idle candidate and guides only rendering continuity and right-facing side-view presentation.
Create ONE new fixed pose of the exact SH4 male Sniffer Dog in the onset of its documented forward lunge and bite: low elongated torso surging toward the RIGHT, jaws open, front paws lifted forward, rear paws pushing off. Preserve one canine head, two visible ear structures, yellow patchy fur, the very long red tongue and exactly FOUR legs. Keep the source's hunched shoulders and lean rear body; do not borrow female earless anatomy or purple tongue. The whole tongue curves with the motion and stays entirely in frame. Clear silhouette, no victim or second character.
Maintain the source identity and restrained game-render material detail. A single still for forwardSpecial, not a movement cycle or animation sheet. True transparent RGBA background. Center the entire subject in the middle 60 percent of the canvas, with generous clear margin on EVERY edge; show every paw, claw, ear and tongue tip. No scenery, ground plane, cast shadow, lettering, effects, blood spray, new wounds or extra limbs.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one fixed full-body combat sprite for an existing 2D fighting-game character.

Create ONE new fixed pose of this exact Carrion at the onset of its documented bodily lunge: its low folded front mass thrust toward the LEFT and downward, thick contorted trunk pitched slightly forward, visible rear supporting limb bent and pushing from the floor. Preserve the compact folded torso, recessed indistinct head, fleshy mottled red-brown surface, and the unusual supporting limbs seen in the references. Keep the distant side naturally occluded; do not invent a canine muzzle, dog ears, tail, claws, horns, extra limbs, a human face or weapons. This is a modest compression and forward surge of the same silhouette, not a new anatomical form. No victim, contact damage or second creature.
Single static forwardSpecial image, not a cycle or sheet. True transparent RGBA background. Complete body centered within the middle 60 percent of the canvas with clear margin on ALL sides, no cropped tips. Match the restrained detailed game-render treatment of the supplied idle. No scenery, ground plane, cast shadow, text, motion trails, blood spray or added injury.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one fixed full-body combat sprite for an existing 2D fighting-game character.
Image 1 is the original PlayStation Silent Hill 1999 Creeper model, controlling anatomy and identity. Image 2 is the existing project right-facing side-view idle, controlling the low camera and rendering continuity.
Create ONE new static crawling pose of this exact SH1 Creeper facing RIGHT: low elongated closed abdomen, the near foreleg reaching forward and down while the other foreleg is bent back, the smaller legs offset into a readable crawling step. Preserve exactly SIX legs total including the two large jointed forelegs, the original mottled dark olive-brown shell, two fine antennae and the two long rear filaments. Keep the complete appendages connected to the correct body segments. It remains one insect, not a swarm, and keeps the closed shell with no opened wings. Retain the low side-on camera of the project sprite, allowing the far legs to overlap naturally.
One fixed walk image, not a loop, multi-pose sheet or animation. True transparent RGBA background. Center the entire subject in the middle 60 percent of the canvas, leaving at least generous clear margins on ALL sides including antennae and trailing filaments. Soft readable game-render lighting. No scenery, floor, cast shadow, UI, text, duplicate insects, motion trails or new anatomical parts.
